actions.action: Repot in fresh, loose, breathable soil
Cut under the bark with a knife to check whether the stem or trunk inside is green or yellow
If rotten, cut away rotten upper branches or stem sections down to healthy green tissue
Unpot the plant and trim away all rotted roots
If the trunk is shriveled, cut it, remove the leaves and replant the healthy part

verdict.reason: The answer mentions underwatering only briefly and frames the main problem as poor aeration and root rot; its repotting advice partly matches the fix but omits a thorough soak, and its advice to cut into a dehydrated soft stem as if it were rot could harm the plant and delay watering.
